text.p: Swedish insurer Skandia on Friday said it was analysing the rival bids for Stadshypotek and was continuing to prepare its prospectus for a proposed merger with the mortgage bank.

"Preparations ahead of Skandia's extraordinary general meeting scheduled for Thursday, December 19, 1996, as well as the work to prepare Skandia's prospectus to the shareholders in Stradshypotek continue according to plan," Skandia said in a statement.
Skandia's chairman Sven Soderberg, said the company was analysing the current situation after Handelsbanken's bid for Stadshypotek on Thursday.
"Skandia is consequently analysing the current situation," Soderberg said.
A Skandia spokesman said more information on the situation would be released early next week.
Skandia and Stadshypotek on November 25 announced a proposed merger that valued Sweden's largest mortgage lender at about 21 billion crowns.
But the government voiced fierce opposition to the proposal and continued with plans to sell its 34 percent in Stadshypotek through a controlled auction.
Handelsbanken on Thursday announced a takeover bid valuing Stadshypotek at 22.9 billion crowns which the government gave preliminary approval on the condition that no higher bids are received.
